title: UART overview: direct logic link or external transceiver
summary: Select a direct logic link, debug header or external physical layer. Confirm directions, voltage compatibility, baud and framing.
applies_to: Asynchronous logic-level UART/USART unless an external physical layer is explicitly selected.
required_inputs: On-board or external connection and flow-control requirements
verification: Read both endpoint specifications and verify a complete frame at the receiver.
limitations: Synchronous USART, LIN and single-wire modes need separate patterns. Do not assume a universal baud-error tolerance.

citations.locator: Interface and Data Transmission, pages 1-2; only connectivity and framing guidance used

title: UART direct TX-to-RX pattern
summary: Connect each transmitter to the other endpoint's receiver with compatible logic levels and a shared reference.
applies_to: Asynchronous logic-level UART/USART unless an external physical layer is explicitly selected.
required_inputs: TX/RX pin directions, framing and oscillator/baud-divider errors
verification: Measure baud, framing and receiver voltage at operating corners.
limitations: TX and RX are independent single-ended nets, not a differential pair; length matching is not a general UART requirement.

citations.locator: Interface and Data Transmission, pages 1-2; only connectivity and framing guidance used

pattern.diagram:
A.TX ---> B.RX
A.RX <--- B.TX
A.GND --- B.GND
placement: Place endpoints to allow short, direct routes.
routing: Keep TX and RX clear of noisy switching nodes; apply the linked return-path guidance.
return_path: Carry a shared reference between endpoints.
pitfalls: Matching baud settings does not prove that clock errors fit the receiver budget.

title: UART logic-level debug header pattern
summary: Label the header from the board's perspective, including its logic voltage and ground. Verify the adapter before connection.
applies_to: Asynchronous logic-level UART/USART unless an external physical layer is explicitly selected.
required_inputs: Adapter pinout, voltage and whether its power pin supplies or senses power
verification: Audit pin directions and check for unintended powering through the adapter.
limitations: A USB-to-UART adapter is not necessarily voltage-compatible. Power connection is an explicit system decision.

citations.locator: Interface and Data Transmission, pages 1-2; only connectivity and framing guidance used
GPIO functional description and GPIO hardware configuration; apply with the selected STM32 datasheet

pattern.diagram:
Board.TX ---> Adapter.RX
Board.RX <--- Adapter.TX
Board.GND --- Adapter.GND
Power: connect only after supply-role review
placement: Place the header accessibly; place chosen protection at the connector boundary.
routing: Route protected signals onward without bypassing protection; see esd-flow-through.
return_path: Include a ground conductor beside the signal path through the cable.
pitfalls: Do not infer TX/RX direction from an unlabeled cable or connect supply pins blindly.

title: UART external physical-layer pattern
summary: Use an appropriate transceiver when the external link requires RS-232 or RS-485 electrical signaling.
applies_to: Asynchronous logic-level UART/USART unless an external physical layer is explicitly selected.
required_inputs: Chosen physical layer, cable, grounding and transceiver
Direction control for half-duplex operation if applicable
verification: Verify logic-side compatibility and the selected physical-layer termination and protection.
limitations: RS-232 and RS-485 are alternatives with different electrical requirements; neither connects directly to MCU UART pins.

citations.locator: RS-485 physical-layer, termination and bus topology sections

pattern.diagram:
MCU UART <--> selected transceiver <--> connector <--> cable
RS-232 OR RS-485: choose and document the physical layer
placement: Place the transceiver and selected protection near the cable entry.
routing: Follow the chosen physical-layer routing guide and its device datasheet.
return_path: Design signal reference, ground offset and any isolation explicitly.
pitfalls: Do not apply RS-485 termination to an RS-232 link.
